text:
Data from sampling by Applicant (Duke Power Company, 1976e) from October 1975 - July 1976 show brown trout to dominate with black crappie, largemouth bass, rainbow trout, and carp comprising most of the remainder of the fish caught. The latter data (202 fish) show brown trout (mean weight = 3.67 lbs.) representing 43.1 percent by number and 74.0 percent by weight of the fish collected, while rainbow trout (mean weight = 0.47 lbs.) represented 5.9 percent by number and 3.5 percent by weight of the samples. Black crappie made up 28.2 percent by number and 6.2 percent by weight of the catch, and largemouth bass (mean weight = 0.92 lbs) comprised 10.4 percent by number and 4.5 percent by weight of the fish taken.
Frame trawl sampling conducted in March - September 1975 for young-of-the-year fishes yielded yellow perch (Perca flavescens), black crappie, sunfish (bluegill, warm-mouth, redbreast, spotted, and redear), and threadfin shad. The greatest density in trawl catches occurred in the Whitewater Arm of Jocassee, with lesser densities in the Toxaway River Arm and dam area. Black crappie were also numerous at the dam station.
Creel census data for 1974, (Table 2-9) show estimates of total catch in Lake Jocassee. Bluegill was the dominant species in the creels, followed by largemouth bass, rainbow trout, and crappies (based on total numbers). Pickerel, catfishes, and carp were also present, but their combined numbers were less than one percent of the total catch. The replacement value of the 1974 catch in Lake Jocassee was estimated at $59,782 (South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department, 1976).
The absence of figures for brown trout and the numbers for rainbow trout in the Lake Jocassee Creel census data are to some extent misleading in that they represent only daytime sampling. However, fishing pressure in Lake Jocassee is heavy at night, especially in the vicinity of the inlet-outlet towers to the Jocassee pumped storage facility. Trout fishing is reported to be especially good during periods when this facility is in the pumping mode, and fishermen are undoubtedly taking some trout from the lake. Creel census procedures are reportedly being altered to include this nighttime fishing pressure.
